normalized_mechanism: Legislative powers granted by the Constitution are vested in the Congress of the United States.
negative_condition: Legislative authority is not established outside the identified constitutional grant and vested institution.

normalized_mechanism: Congress is constitutionally constituted as two distinct chambers: the Senate and the House of Representatives.
negative_condition: Neither chamber alone constitutes the whole Congress where the Constitution assigns authority to Congress as the bicameral institution.

normalized_mechanism: House membership authority originates through recurring selection by the People of the several States.
negative_condition: House membership is not constitutionally constituted through an alternative selector under this source clause.

normalized_mechanism: Eligibility to participate as a House elector in each State is bounded by the qualifications required for electors of that State's most numerous legislative branch.
negative_condition: A House elector qualification exceeding or departing from the constitutionally linked State qualification is not established by this clause.

normalized_mechanism: Eligibility for service as a Representative is bounded by minimum age, citizenship duration, and State inhabitancy requirements.
negative_condition: A person failing any stated qualification is not constitutionally qualified under this clause.

normalized_mechanism: Representation and direct-tax apportionment operate among the States according to the population rule stated in the source text.
negative_condition: Apportionment under this clause is not established outside the identified interstate allocation domain and stated counting rule.

normalized_mechanism: The constitutional enumeration is temporally bounded and its manner is subject to direction by law.
negative_condition: Enumeration timing or manner outside the stated constitutional schedule and lawful direction is not authorized by this clause.

normalized_mechanism: The number of Representatives is bounded by a maximum ratio of one Representative for every thirty thousand persons under this source rule.
negative_condition: Representation exceeding the stated maximum ratio is not authorized by this clause.

normalized_mechanism: Each State is guaranteed at least one Representative under the stated apportionment structure.
negative_condition: A State receiving zero Representatives is inconsistent with this source clause.

normalized_mechanism: Before completion of the first enumeration, representation is allocated among the named States according to the source's transitional allocation.
negative_condition: The transitional allocation does not establish authority beyond the named States, quantities, or stated pre-enumeration period.

normalized_mechanism: When a vacancy occurs in a State's House representation, that State's Executive Authority is vested with the duty to issue election writs to fill the vacancy.
negative_condition: The vacancy condition does not vest the writ-issuing function in an unidentified or different principal under this clause.

normalized_mechanism: The House of Representatives is vested with authority to choose its Speaker and other officers.
negative_condition: This clause does not vest selection of House officers in an external principal.

normalized_mechanism: The power of impeachment is allocated exclusively to the House of Representatives.
negative_condition: Another constitutional actor may not substitute for the House in exercising the sole impeachment power under this clause.

normalized_mechanism: The Senate is structurally constituted by equal State representation, with two Senators from each State and the term stated in the source.
negative_condition: Senate composition under this clause is not constituted by unequal State seat allocation.

normalized_mechanism: Each Senator's voting authority is bounded to one vote.
negative_condition: A Senator is not granted more than one vote by this clause.

normalized_mechanism: Following the first election, Senators are procedurally divided as equally as possible into three classes.
negative_condition: The initial classification process is not authorized outside the stated three-class structure.

normalized_mechanism: Senate class terms are temporally staggered so that approximately one third of seats become selectable every second year.
negative_condition: The initial class expiration schedule is not established outside the stated second-, fourth-, and sixth-year sequence.

normalized_mechanism: During the stated vacancy and legislative-recess condition, a State Executive may make a temporary Senate appointment until the legislature next meets.
negative_condition: Temporary appointment authority does not exist under this clause absent the stated vacancy/recess conditions or beyond the stated temporary duration.

normalized_mechanism: Eligibility for service as a Senator is bounded by minimum age, citizenship duration, and State inhabitancy requirements.
negative_condition: A person failing any stated qualification is not constitutionally qualified under this clause.

normalized_mechanism: The Vice President serves as President of the Senate but lacks ordinary voting authority, with a vote permitted only when the Senate is equally divided.
negative_condition: The Vice President may not exercise an ordinary Senate vote absent the stated equal-division condition.

normalized_mechanism: The Senate is vested with authority to choose its other officers and a President pro tempore under the stated Vice-Presidential absence or succession conditions.
negative_condition: The President-pro-tempore selection condition is not established outside the stated circumstances.

normalized_mechanism: The power to try impeachments is allocated exclusively to the Senate.
negative_condition: Another constitutional actor may not substitute for the Senate in exercising the sole impeachment-trial power under this clause.

normalized_mechanism: When the Senate sits for an impeachment trial, its members are procedurally bound to act under oath or affirmation.
negative_condition: The impeachment-trial procedure established by this clause does not omit the oath-or-affirmation requirement.

normalized_mechanism: When the President is tried by the Senate, presiding authority is assigned to the Chief Justice.
negative_condition: Ordinary Senate presiding authority does not substitute for the Chief Justice under the stated presidential-impeachment condition.

normalized_mechanism: Impeachment conviction requires concurrence of two thirds of the Senate members present.
negative_condition: Impeachment conviction is not established below the stated two-thirds concurrence threshold.

normalized_mechanism: The effect of an impeachment judgment is negatively bounded to removal from office and disqualification from covered federal office.
negative_condition: An impeachment judgment may not extend beyond the effects permitted by this clause.

normalized_mechanism: Impeachment conviction does not replace or extinguish separate criminal indictment, trial, judgment, and punishment according to law.
negative_condition: Impeachment adjudication does not silently become or displace the distinct criminal-law authority class.

normalized_mechanism: State legislatures hold the initial authority to prescribe the times, places, and manner of congressional elections within their respective States.
negative_condition: A State legislature's authority under this clause is not established outside its constitutionally applicable election-regulation domain.

normalized_mechanism: Congress may by law make or alter State congressional-election regulations, subject to the source's stated exception concerning places of choosing Senators.
negative_condition: Congressional alteration authority does not extend through this clause to the stated excluded subject.

normalized_mechanism: Congress is temporally required to assemble at least once each year, with the source establishing a default meeting day subject to lawful alteration.
negative_condition: Congressional assembly frequency may not fall below the constitutional minimum established by this clause.

normalized_mechanism: Each House has exclusive institutional jurisdiction to judge the elections, returns, and qualifications of its own members.
negative_condition: One House does not obtain jurisdiction under this clause to judge membership matters belonging to the other House.

normalized_mechanism: A majority of each House constitutes the quorum required to conduct business.
negative_condition: Ordinary House or Senate business is not constitutionally established through a quorum below the stated majority threshold.

normalized_mechanism: A number smaller than a quorum is granted the limited authority to adjourn from day to day.
negative_condition: The smaller-number authority established here does not itself confer the full business authority requiring a quorum.

normalized_mechanism: A smaller number may compel attendance of absent members only under authority and in the manner and penalties provided by the respective House.
negative_condition: Compulsory attendance authority is not established outside the House-defined authorization, manner, and penalty conditions.

normalized_mechanism: Each House is granted authority to determine the rules governing its own proceedings.
negative_condition: One House does not obtain rulemaking authority over the proceedings of the other through this clause.

normalized_mechanism: Each House is granted authority to punish its own members for disorderly behavior.
negative_condition: The disciplinary authority established by this clause is bounded to the House's own members and the stated disciplinary subject.
